content.title: Women's March Madness First Four recap: Virginia defeats Arizona State
content.text: March 19, 2026Updated March 20, 2026, 9:15 a.m. ETThe Women's NCAA Tournament is off and running with the First Four games in the books.Southern defeated Samford, 65-53, on Thursday at the Colonial Life Arena in Columbia, South Carolina, marking the program's second-consecutive First Four win. The Jaguars locked down the No. 16 seed in the Sacramento 4 bracket and earned a first-round matchup against No. 1 seed South Carolina.Meanwhile, No. 7 Georgia will play No. 10 Virginia in the first-round after the Cavaliers defeated Arizona State, 57-55, on Thursday.On Wednesday, Nebraska and Missouri State advanced in the first two games of the First Four. No. 11 Nebraska secured a first-round matchup against No. 6 seed Baylor, while Missouri State earned the No. 16 seed in the Fort Worth 3 bracket and a first-round date with the No. 1 seed Texas Longhorns.USA TODAY Sports provided live updates, highlights and scores from Thursday's NCAA First Four games. Catch up on both matchups below: Women's First Four scheduleWednesday, March 18Nebraska 75, Richmond 56Missouri State 85, Stephen F. Austin 75Thursday, March 19Southern 65, Samford 53Virginia 57, Arizona State 55 Virginia vs. Arizona State live updates Final: Virginia 57, Arizona State 55The final minute was a fight to the finish for the last remaining spot in the round of 64.Arizona State's Marley Washenitz knocked down a 3-pointer with 41.0 seconds remaining to tie it up at 51. Virginia's Kymora Johnson responded with a 3-pointer of her own with 30 seconds remaining to retake the lead, 54-51."It's March and I was like, they're backing up. I'm going to shoot it," Johnson said. "That's what shooters do. Keep shooting. Obviously not a great day for us from the field. ... But my teammates believe in me. They knew I could hit that shot, so I took it."Arizona State's defense came up clutch with a turnover with 20 seconds remaining and Heloisa Carrera made a layup to come within one point of Virginia, 54-53. The Sun Devils fouled and Caitlin Weimar hit both free throws to extend their lead to three points with 11 seconds left. Arizona's Joyah Lovett made a quick layup and Virginia's Johnson hit another free throw before the final buzzer sounded and the Cavaliers won, 57-55.Johnson finished with a double-double with 17 points and 10 rebounds.End of Q3: Virginia 40, Arizona State 36Arizona State outscored Virginia 14-10 in the third quarter to cut its deficit to four heading into the fourth.Both team’s stars are struggling. Gabby Elliott, Arizona State’s leading scorer this season, has four points and is shooting 1-of-9 from the field and 0-of-2 from the 3-point line. Elliott is wearing a large brace one her right leg after injuring her knee in February. Kymora Johnson, Virginia’s leading scorer, is shooting 3-of-13 from the field and 1-of-6 from the 3-point line. She has 10 points and is the only Virginia player to reach double digits. Arizona State’s Marley Washenitz has a team-high 11 points, but has been limited to 18 minutes with four fouls. Halftime: Virginia 30, Arizona State 22Virginia has an eight-point leading over Arizona State heading into halftime after holding the Sun Devils to their second-lowest scoring half of the season. Both teams have struggled from the floor. Arizona State missed 11 of their last 12 field goals, while Virginia missed 10 of their last 12. But turnovers and rebounds have marked the difference. Virginia has scored seven points off seven ASU turnovers and is outrebounding the Sun Devils, 23-17.Romi Levy has eight points for the Cavaliers. McKinna Brackens has nine points for Arizona State. Flagrant 1 foul calledVirginia senior forward Tabitha Amanze made a rookie mistake that resulted in a Flagrant 1 foul. Amanze tapped Arizona State's Jyah LoVett on the head after LoVett stole the ball from her. The foul wasn’t initially called on the floor, but Arizona State head coach Molly Miller asked the referees to review at the contact. It resulted in a Flagrant 1 foul and two free-throw attempts for the Sun Devils. Last-Tear Poa knocked down one of two free throw attempts to come within seven point of Virginia, 24-17. Check out Molly Miller's jacketArizona State head coach Molly Miller wore a custom jacket that featured her players' signatures. End of Q1: Virginia 19, Arizona State 14Virginia is shooting lights out to start, going 54% from the field and 2-of-3 from the 3-point line. Six different players have scored for Virginia, led by five points from Romi Levy, and have a five-point lead.Arizona State went more than four minutes without scoring before Gabby Elliot made a layup with 0:01 seconds remaining in the quarter to end Virginia’s 7-0 run. Marley Washenitz has a team-high six points. Virginia vs. Arizona State underwayThe First Four matchup between Virginia and Arizona State is underway at Carver-Hawkeye Arena in Iowa City, Iowa. The winner will lock down the No. 10 seed in the Sacramento 4 bracket and secure a first-round matchup with No. 7 Georgia. Virginia has a 14-12 lead over Arizona State with 3:00 remaining in the first quarter. Romi Levy has five points for the Cavaliers, while Arizona State's Marley Washenitz (6) knocked down a pair of 3-pointers. Defense, belief fuels Arizona State’s surge under Molly MillerIn her first season as women's basketball coach, Molly Miller has transformed a losing program into a contender. Arizona State opened the 2025-26 season with a program-best 15 consecutive wins, tying the school record. The Sun Devils finished the regular season 29-10 and 9-9 the Big 12, better than last season's 3-15 conference record."I told 'em the other day, I'm like, 'You've already flipped it now. The hard part is sustaining success,'" Miller told USA TODAY Sports about her squad's turnaround. "When you're facing a conference with such parody in any given night, a win or a loss can have March implications. The Big 12 isn't going to reward potential, it's going to reward night in, night out, daily grind." The No. 16 seed Jaguars will take on top seed South Carolina on Saturday. This will be the first meeting between the teams.The Jaguars are one of two HBCUs to advance to NCAA Tournament play this year. The other, No. 14 seed Howard University, will play No. 3 seed Ohio State on Saturday.Southern also advanced to the NCAA Tournament last year, beating UC San Diego in the First Four before falling to UCLA in the first round. The Jaguars have now made it to the tournament in three of the last four seasons.Southern and Samford entered the fourth quarter tied at 44. Southern scored eight unanswered points to pull away midway through the quarter. Jaylia Reed was the leading scorer with 16 points. DeMya Porter finished the game with a double-double with 15 points and 12 rebounds. Briana Rivera led Samford with 16 points. - Ella Sather End of Q3: Samford 44, Southern 44We are all tied up following a back-and-forth matchup that's featured eight ties and 10 lead changes. Ten minutes is all that separates Samford or Southern from the field of 64.Samford's Briana Rivera has a game-high 14 points. Rivera, who leads the nation in made 3-pointers (299) entering Thursday, has connected for 3-of-7 3-pointers. Jaylia Reed has 10 points for Southern. South Carolina watches First Four gameNo. 1 seed South Carolina doesn't tip off March Madness until Saturday, but head coach Dawn Staley and her squad were front and center at the Colonial Life Arena to scout the competition. Ta'Niya Latson, Joyce Edwards, Tessa Johnson and Raven Johnson were spotted in the crowd at the First Four matchup between Samford vs. Southern on Thursday. The winner earns the No. 16 seed in the Sacramento 4 bracket and will face South Carolina in the first round. Halftime: Southern 27, Samford 24Southern holds a one-possession lead at halftime against Samford in their First Four game at Colonial Life Arena. The winner advances to a first-round matchup against top-seeded South Carolina on Saturday. The Jaguars, with nine steals in the first half, scored two of their 3-pointers off turnovers. Southern’s Jocelyn Tate leads the team with six points off the bench. Samford is staying in the game with well-timed 3-pointers, making five of 15 in the first half. − Ella Sather Q1: Southern 11, Samford 8Points are hard to come by so far and both teams are showing early nerves. Southern used a 9-2 run to take a seven-point lead over Samford, but the Bulldogs closed the quarter on a 6-2 run to come within three points heading into the second quarter. Both teams are shooting a dismal 25% from the field and 3-point line. Samford has five turnovers, yet they are within striking range. Francie Morris has six of Samford’s eight points. Samford vs. Southern underwayThe First Four matchup between Samford and Southern is underway at Colonial Life Arena in Columbia, South Carolina. The winner will lock down the No. 16 seed in the Sacramento 4 bracket and secure a first-round matchup with No. 1 seed South Carolina. Emily Snoddy got Samford on the board first, but Southern went on a 9-0 run to take a 9-2 lead with 5:32 remaining in the first quarter. Jaylia Reed has a game-high three points for Southern. Henderson: Arizona StateHeather Burns: VirginiaNancy Armour: Virginia Molly Miller rejoins Arizona State after illnessArizona State is playing in the Women’s NCAA Tournament this week for the first time in seven years after putting together a 24-10 overall record under first-year head coach Molly Miller. But when the Sun Devils arrived in Iowa City, Iowa ahead of their First Four matchup with Virginia, Miller wasn’t with them.An Arizona State spokesperson confirmed to USA TODAY Sports that Miller is dealing with an illness and did not make the trip to Iowa City. However, Miller rejoined her team on Thursday ahead of for their tournament opener against Virginia, which tips off at 9 p.m. ET on ESPN2. Read full story here. Juju Watkins injury update: Is she playing in March Madness?No. 9 seed USC is set to open March Madness against No. 8 Clemson, but they'll be without guard Juju Watkins. She was ruled out the entire season. Watkins said she'll "sit out this season and fully focus on continuing to recover" after suffering a torn right ACL in the second round of the 2025 NCAA tournament on March 24. Who is playing in the First Four of Women's March Madness?Nebraska vs. Richmond and Stephen F. Austin vs. Missouri State played on March 18. Nebraska and Missouri State advanced.Virginia vs. Arizona State and Samford vs. Southern play Thursday, March 19. When is the Women's First Four?Half of the First Four was played Wednesday, March 18. The second two game are Thursday, March 19.It's the official start of the Women's NCAA Tournament. Eight teams will compete in the play-in games to determine which two teams will punch their tickets to the dance.Once the bracket has been cut down from 68 teams to the final 64-team field, the first round will begin on Friday, March 20.Women's March Madness scheduleBelow are all the dates for the 2026 women's NCAA Tournament:First Four: Wednesday, March 18 through Thursday, March 19First Round: Friday, March 20 through Saturday, March 21Second Round: Sunday, March 22 through Monday, March 23Sweet 16: Friday, March 27 through Saturday, March 29Elite Eight: Sunday, March 29 through Monday, March 30Final Four: Friday, April 3National championship: Sunday, April 5 Women's March Madness bracketThe USA TODAY Sports Bracket Challenge is back, with a $1 million grand prize for a perfect bracket.
